records.literal_gloss: For the director, on mahalath, a maskil of David.

en.L: For the director: on mahalath. A maskil of David.
en.B: For the music director. On mahalath. A maskil of David.
en.R: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Mahalath". A song by David to teach and give insight.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: mahalath: a musical term whose meaning is unknown
decisions.reason: The word (machalat) appears only here and in the title of Psalm 88. It may be the name of a tune, or come from a word for sickness or sorrow; its meaning is lost.

decisions.choice: maskil: probably a skillful or instructive song
decisions.reason: As in 32:1, the word (maskil) comes from a verb meaning to be wise or to give insight. Its exact sense as a kind of song is no longer known.

decisions.choice: To the tune "Mahalath"
decisions.reason: Readable takes the term as a tune name, as with other such terms (45:1).

decisions.choice: a song to teach and give insight
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the term, as in 42:1.

source.text: אָ֘מַ֤ר נָבָ֣ל בְּ֭לִבּוֹ אֵ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֑ים הִֽ֝שְׁחִ֗יתוּ וְהִֽתְעִ֥יבוּ עָ֝֗וֶל אֵ֣ין עֹֽשֵׂה־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: Says [the] fool in his heart, There is no God. They have acted corruptly and done abominable injustice; there is none who does good.

en.L: The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." \q They have acted corruptly, \q and they have done abominable injustice; \q there is none who does good.
en.B: Fools tell themselves, "There is no God." \q They are rotten through and through; \q their wrongdoing is detestable. \q Not one of them does good.
en.R: Foolish people think, "There is no God." \q They are evil, and they do terrible, unfair things. \q None of them does what is good.

decisions.choice: Psalm 14 and Romans 3
decisions.reason: This psalm is almost the same as Psalm 14. It says "God" where Psalm 14 has "the LORD", has "injustice" for "deeds" in this verse, and has a different verse 6. Paul quotes verses 2-4 in Romans 3:10-12 to show that all people are under sin.

decisions.choice: the fool: one who lives without regard for God
decisions.reason: As in 14:1, the fool (naval) is not slow of mind but morally senseless, living as if God does not matter (1 Samuel 25:25).

decisions.choice: There is no God: living as if God will not act
decisions.reason: To say something "in the heart" is to think it. As in 14:1, the fool is living as if God will never see or judge, not arguing about whether he exists.

decisions.choice: injustice: wrong done to others
decisions.reason: The word ('awel) is injustice, unfair dealing. Psalm 14:1 has "deeds" here.

decisions.choice: Fools ... they (B); Foolish people (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes one figure ("he", "his") who stands for everyone who acts this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, as Psalm 10 does with "the wicked", which includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

source.text: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים מִשָּׁמַיִם֮ הִשְׁקִ֪יף עַֽל־בְּנֵ֫י אָדָ֥ם לִ֭רְאוֹת הֲיֵ֣שׁ מַשְׂכִּ֑יל דֹּ֝רֵ֗שׁ אֶת־אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: God from heaven looks down on [the] children of humankind to see [whether] there is [one] who has insight, who seeks God.

en.L: God from heaven looks down on the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}} \q to see whether there is [anyone] who has insight, \q who seeks God.
en.B: From heaven God looks down on the human race \q to see whether anyone is wise, \q anyone who is looking for God.
en.R: God watches all people from heaven. \q He wants to see if anyone is wise and wants to know God.

decisions.choice: God: where Psalm 14 has the LORD
decisions.reason: Psalms 42-83 often say "God" ('elohim) where other psalms use the divine name. Psalm 14:2 has "the LORD" here; this psalm has "God" in every place where Psalm 14 has the name. The words here follow the Hebrew of this psalm.

decisions.choice: God looks down to see: as before the flood and at Babel
decisions.reason: As in 14:2: God sees the earth before the flood (Genesis 6:5, 12) and comes down to see the tower of Babel (Genesis 11:5). He looks before he judges.

decisions.choice: who has insight: who acts wisely
decisions.reason: The word (maskil) is the same as the term in the title (verse 1): someone who understands and so acts rightly.

decisions.choice: children of humankind, with "sons of men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 11:4.

decisions.choice: wants to know God
decisions.reason: Readable says what seeking God means.

source.text: כֻּלּ֥וֹ סָג֮ יַחְדָּ֪ו נֶ֫אֱלָ֥חוּ אֵ֤ין עֹֽשֵׂה־ט֑וֹב אֵ֝֗ין גַּם־אֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: All of it has turned back; together they have gone sour; there is none who does good, there is not even one.

en.L: All of it has turned back; together they have gone sour; \q there is none who does good, \q not even one.
en.B: Everyone has turned away; all alike have gone bad. \q No one does good, \q not a single one.
en.R: Everyone has turned away from God. All of them have become rotten. \q No one does what is good. \q Not even one person!

decisions.choice: turned back: turned away from God
decisions.reason: The verb (sug) means to move back, to turn away. Psalm 14:3 has a similar word, "turned aside".

decisions.choice: gone sour: become rotten
decisions.reason: As in 14:3, the verb ('alach) is used of what has spoiled and become foul (Job 15:16).

decisions.choice: all of it: the whole human race
decisions.reason: "It" refers to humankind, "the children of humankind" of verse 3, taken as one body.

decisions.choice: from God
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they have turned from (m1).

decisions.choice: All of it
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular "it" of the Hebrew (m3).

source.text: הֲלֹ֥א יָדְעוּ֮ פֹּ֤עֲלֵ֫י אָ֥וֶן אֹכְלֵ֣י עַ֭מִּי אָ֣כְלוּ לֶ֑חֶם אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א קָרָֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not they know, workers of wickedness, eaters of my people [who] eat bread? God they do not call on.

en.L: Do they not know, the workers of wickedness, \q who eat up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people [as] they eat bread? \q On God they do not call.
en.B: Have they learned nothing, these evildoers? \q They devour {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people as if they were eating bread, \q and they never call on God.
en.R: Do these evil people understand nothing? \q They destroy {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people as easily as they eat a meal. \q They never pray to God.

decisions.choice: my people: God's people, God speaking
decisions.reason: As in 14:4, "my people" is most naturally God's own word for Israel, spoken in the middle of the psalmist's words.

decisions.choice: eat my people as they eat bread: destroy them without a thought
decisions.reason: The wicked consume God's people as casually as they sit down to a meal (Micah 3:3).

decisions.choice: call on God: pray to him
decisions.reason: To call on God is to turn to him in prayer and worship (Genesis 4:26).

source.text: שָׁ֤ם׀פָּֽחֲדוּ־פַחַד֮ לֹא־הָ֪יָה֫ פָ֥חַד כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֗ים פִּ֭זַּר עַצְמ֣וֹת חֹנָ֑ךְ הֱ֝בִשֹׁ֗תָה כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים מְאָסָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: There they dreaded [with] dread, [where] there was no dread, for God has scattered [the] bones of [the one] encamping [against] you; you have put [them] to shame, for God has rejected them.

en.L: There they dreaded [with] dread [where] there had been no dread, \q for God scattered the bones of the one encamped [against] you; \q you put [them] to shame, for God had rejected them.
en.B: Terror gripped them there, where there had been nothing to fear, \q for God scattered the bones of the army camped against you. \q You brought them to shame, because God had thrown them aside.
en.R: But then they were suddenly terrified, though there had been nothing to be afraid of. \q God scattered the bones of the enemies who camped around you, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. \q You made them look like fools, because God had thrown them away.

decisions.choice: Psalm 14 differs here
decisions.reason: Psalm 14:5-6 shares many of the same letters but says something different: God is with the righteous and is the refuge of the poor. Here God has scattered the attackers. The two forms of the psalm were sung for different occasions.

decisions.choice: where there was no dread: terror without a cause
alternatives: such terror as there had never been
decisions.reason: The enemies were seized with panic though nothing they could see threatened them: God himself struck them with fear. The verbs are in the past form, as often in prophecy, for what is certain to happen.

decisions.choice: scattered the bones: the attackers lie dead and unburied
decisions.reason: To lie unburied, with bones scattered, was the final disgrace (141:7; Jeremiah 8).

decisions.choice: you: God's people
alternatives: you (God) have put them to shame
decisions.reason: "You" in "encamping against you" is feminine, most likely Zion or the people; "you have put to shame" is masculine and most likely speaks to Israel. Since God is named in the third person in the same line, the people, not God, are addressed.

decisions.choice: his people
decisions.reason: Readable names who is addressed (m4).

source.text: מִ֥י יִתֵּ֣ן מִצִּיּוֹן֮ יְשֻׁע֪וֹת יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל בְּשׁ֣וּב אֱ֭לֹהִים שְׁב֣וּת עַמּ֑וֹ יָגֵ֥ל יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב יִשְׂמַ֥ח יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Who will give from Zion [the] salvations of Israel! When returns God [the] fortunes of his people, may Jacob rejoice, may Israel be glad.

en.L: Who will give from Zion the salvation of Israel! \q When God restores the fortunes of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.
en.B: If only Zion would send Israel its rescue! \q When God turns back the fortunes of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q let Jacob shout for joy and Israel be glad.
en.R: How I wish that help would come from Zion and save Israel! \q When God makes life good again for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q the people of Jacob will shout for joy, and Israel will celebrate.

decisions.choice: Who will give: if only
decisions.reason: "Who will give ...?" is the Hebrew way of expressing a wish (14:7; Deuteronomy 5:29).

decisions.choice: salvation: full rescue
decisions.reason: The word is plural here (yeshu'ot), "salvations": rescue in every form. Psalm 14:7 has the singular.

decisions.choice: restores the fortunes: brings back the good days
decisions.reason: As in 14:7, the phrase (shuv shevut) is used where no exile is in view (Job 42:10): God turns a people's ruin into blessing.

decisions.choice: let Jacob rejoice: a wish or a promise
decisions.reason: The verbs can be read as wishes or as statements about the future; Readable says what will happen, which comes to the same.
